newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUGUST 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUGUST 15.

text.p: PRAVO - People in cooperative housing who have asked to have the right of ownership to their name may receive their property for free according to an amendment to the law on housing ownership, proposed by the Minister for Regional Development, Tomas Kvapil.

- Nomura International, to which the Czech government intends to sell over one third of Investicni a Postovni Banka, is planning on developing its activities in the area of small banking, according to Nomura's general manager, Randall Dillard. The statement countered recent speculation that Nomura would sell the small banking division to a foreign company.

- Czech Railways will be given a provisional loan of 875 million crowns. Currently the final conditions are being discussed and the contract itself is expected to be signed on August 20, according to the company's general manager, Vladimir Sosna, who did not mention the name of the institution which will be providing the loan.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - If any other company than Bohemia Sekt wins the tender for the privatisation of Jan Becher - Karlovarska Becherovka then Underberg does not intend to come to any agreement regarding a solution to the trademark disagreement between the two companies, according to Underberg's owner, Emil Underberg.
- The chairman of the Czech Social Democratic Party, Milos Zeman, has proposed creating a provisional budget for the flood damages.

- Mid-year statistics regarding the turnover in the main sectors of the Czech economy seem to confirm fears that a majority of companies will have worse economic results in 1997 than in 1996. Mid-year turnover increased by 2.6 percent in industrial companies and 1.9 percent in agricultural companies and decreased by 1.4 percvent in construction companies.
- Damages caused by the recent flooding in Moravia and Silesia in the area of housing should reach an estimated 8 billion crowns, according to Jan Wagner from the Ministry for Regional Development.

- The planned meeting today between the Chinese Minister of Energy and the Czech Minister of Trade and Industry, Karel Kuhnl, has given rise to speculation in industrial circles that the Chinese government will approve a Czech consortium's involvement in the construction of two power plants worth 10 billion crowns.
- Six companies are still vying for the tender for 89 percent of Jan Becher - Karlovarska Becherovka, according to Ludmila Nutilova, press spokeswoman for the Ministry of Finance.

MLADA FRONTA DNES - The pessimistic estimates made three months ago during the monetary crisis regarding the development of the rate of the crown have not been fulfilled. The crown is actually stronger now against the mark than it was at the beginning of June. In spite of this, experts still agree that the crown will weaken in coming months.
- The recent floods in Moravia and Silesia will have long-term effects on the form of several villages and towns, with some even being left completely deserted.
